title.narrative: Tonga Second Fiscal, Disaster, and Climate Resilience Development Policy Operation

description.narrative: The Second Fiscal, Disaster, and Climate Resilience Development Policy Operation Program aims to support the Kingdom of Tonga in strengthening fiscal and debt sustainability and enhancing resilience to climate change and disasters. This operation is the second in a series of two and is designed around two Program Development Objectives (PDO) and Pillars. Pillar 1 focuses on bolstering domestic revenue mobilization, improving the effectiveness of public debt management, and enhancing energy efficiency. These efforts strengthen fiscal and debt sustainability, with energy measures contributing through enhanced public spending efficiency. Pillar 2 supports the government's capacity to prepare for and respond to climate change and disasters. It strengthens community resilience by enhancing the transmission of disaster warnings that relevant stakeholders can understand and act upon. The DPO is proposed as an International Development Association (IDA) Grant for 12 million dollars. The operation aims to strengthen fiscal sustainability and enhance resilience to climate change and disasters. Pillar 1 focuses on reforming tax expenditures (PA1), enhancing public debt management and increasing debt transparency (PA2), and promoting energy efficiency through the adoption of Minimum Energy Performance Standards and Labelling (MEPSL) (PA3). Pillar 2 strengthens Tonga's ability to prepare for and respond to climate change and disasters by: a) supporting the transmission of disaster warnings via the national cell broadcasting system through the Communications Amendment Bill (PA4), and b) establishing a policy framework for multi-hazard early warnings (PA5). These initiatives ensure early warning communications reach vulnerable communities, including women and children in remote areas.
The proposed Development Policy Operation supports the Government of Tonga to: i) strengthen fiscal and debt sustainability, and ii) enhance resilience to climate change and disasters.

title.narrative: 1. Tax revenue as a share of Gross Domestic product (GDP).

comment.narrative: The target has been achieved. This indicator was revised from consumption tax collection to overall tax revenue to align with the WBG Scorecard. Ongoing reforms are expected to sustain progress, including the government's review of tax exemptions outlined in the FY26 budget. The Ministry of Revenue and Customs (MoRC) has established a Policy and Planning Unit, as reflected in its FY26–28 Corporate Plan. Reform efforts began in FY25 with rationalizing tax expenditures in the tourism sector, and MoRC plans to extend reviews to other sectors—such as agriculture and imported vehicles—through this Unit in FY26.

title.narrative: 2. Public and Publicly Guaranteed (PPG) debt as share of GDP.

comment.narrative: The target has been achieved. The public debt ratio remains on a downward path and is currently below the target for set for this results indicator. Although debt repayments are still substantial, they peaked at 3.3 percent of GDP in FY25, declining to 3.2 percent in FY26, and are projected to fall to 1.8 percent by FY29. Repayment obligations are primarely to the Chinese EXIM Bank, linked to on-lent loans to businesses expected to reimburse on schedule.

title.narrative: 4. Share of population covered by Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Plans incorporating climate-induced disasters preparedness and essential gender-based violence (GBV) support services.

comment.narrative: Progress is being made against this target, though results will not yet be reflected until DRM Plans are in place for both Tongatapu and Vava'u. Risk assessments for both have been conducted and progress is being made towards development of the plans. This indicator is expected to be met by the time the program concludes.

title.narrative: 5. Number of people with enhanced resilience to climate risks.

comment.narrative: The target for this indicator has been achieved. With the delivery of the MHEWS policy, Tonga's entire population now benefits from resilience to climate risks.

title.narrative: 6. Number of individuals registered in the social registry database disaggregated by sex and vulnerability status.

comment.narrative: Progress is being made toward the target. The social registry is currently being piloted, with the launch on July 30, 2025, having so far captured additional data of around 7,300 individuals from 1,700 households in Tongatapu. The registry is expected to have verified data for 10,000 individuals from 2,000 households. In addition to the inclusion of the new data from the pilot, the registry is supporting the consolidation of social protection databases, which currently include around 30,000 individuals. Therefore, it is envisaged that the indicator will be met by the closure of the DPO program.

title.narrative: 3. Nationwide efficiency gain through the adaptation of energy-saving appliances

comment.narrative: Implementation of the Minimum Energy Performance and Standard Labelling (MEPSL) regulation is currently pending cabinet approval of the associated Code of Practice. The Code of Practice is under consultation and is expected to be finalized for Cabinet approval by January 2026.
